        If you have some fall DIY chores to tackle, a good set of cordless tools is a must. But you might have noticed that the price of tools has gone up, and getting through your to-do list on a budget might be tough. October Prime Day often spurs competitors to offer their own deals, and Home Depot has marked down some of its tools by up to 50% during its own fall sale. Here are some of the best deals available right now.Best deals on cordless tool sets at Home DepotA cordless tool set can be a good way to save money as you begin to build a DIY tool kit. If you plan to do repairs, like replacing a fence board or fixing railings, or for DIY woodworking projects, a set of cordless tools is a game changer.The Milwaukee 8-tool 18-volt cordless tool set is on sale for $649, 50% off its regular price. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, a ⅜-inch impact wrench, a reciprocating saw, an angle grinder, an oscillating multitool, a circular saw, a work light, two 4-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag.Best deals on powered ratchets and impact wrenches at Home DepotPowered ratchets and impact wrenches are useful for driving nuts for vehicle maintenance or maintenance on home appliances. They can help break a stubborn bolt that’s seized up, as well. Here are some of the best deals on powered ratchets and wrenches.The Ryobi ½-inch 18-volt impact wrench set is on sale for $159, 41% off its usual price. This tool comes with an 18-volt and a 4-amp-hour battery.The Milwaukee 12-volt, ⅜-inch powered ratchet is on sale for $199, 57% off its typical price. This tool comes with two 12-volt, 5-amp-hour batteries and a charger. A powered ratchet is good for getting at bolts in tight spaces because you don’t need space to rotate the handle in order to turn the socket.The Milwaukee 18-volt ½-inch impact wrench is on sale for $299, 35% off its regular price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a Milwaukee 18-volt battery and charger to use it.Best deals on cutting and shaping tools at Home DepotFrom trim to deck boards, every DIY upgrade or repair can be made simpler with the right saws and trimming tools. Cutting custom shapes to install molding around outlets or adding a built-in shelf to your closet requires that your materials be cut to fit. Here are some of the best deals on cutting and shaping tools.The Milwaukee 18-volt sawzall kit is on sale for $199, 45% off its usual price. The set comes with the reciprocating saw, an 18-volt, 5-amp-hour battery, and a charger.The DeWalt 20-volt oscillating multitool set is on sale for $99, 50% off its regular price. This set comes with the multitool, two starter blades, a 1.5-amp-hour battery, and a charger.The Milwaukee 18-volt cordless router set is on sale for $229, 41% off its usual price. This tool comes with a 5-amp-hour battery, but not a charger, so you’ll need a Milwaukee 18-volt battery charger to use it.The Milwaukee 18-volt 6 ½-inch circular saw is on sale for $229, 41% off its regular price. This tool comes with a 5-amp-hour battery, but not a charger, so you’ll need a Milwaukee 18-volt battery charger to use it.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Best deals on batteries and chargers at Home DepotBatteries can be the most expensive part of a cordless tool set, and having enough batteries to keep a fresh one on the charger so you don’t have to wait to swap batteries is a big time-saver. Here are some of the best deals on batteries and chargers.The Milwaukee 18-volt FORGE battery starter set is on sale for $279, 36% off its typical price. The set comes with a 5-amp-hour battery, an 8-amp-hour battery, and a charger.The DeWalt 20-volt XR battery starter set is on sale for $199, 50% off its regular price. The set comes with an 8-amp-hour battery, a 4-amp-hour battery, and a charger.A two-pack of DeWalt 20-volt MAX 6-amp-hour batteries is on sale for $179, 36% off its usual price.When is Prime Day in October?October Prime Day is a two-day event that starts Oct. 6 and ends on Oct. 7.What happens on Amazon Prime Day?On Oct. 6 and Oct. 7, Amazon will have a big online sale for Prime Members with many products going for their lowest price of the year.What goes on sale on Prime Day?Since Prime Big Deal Days happens in the fall, you're likely to see more deals on gaming and indoor gym equipment. Amazon has already announced some of the 35 categories that will be on sale, including beauty, tech, kitchen, fashion, and home. Some brands Amazon has already mentioned are: Shark, Princess Polly, Soundcore by Anker, UGG, Nest New York, Sony, Tarte, Adidas, and Barefoot Dreams.

        Pet hair tends to gather in inconvenient and less conspicuous places—along baseboards, under furniture, and on upholstery—which can make dragging out a full-size upright vacuum feel like more trouble than the mess warrants. The cordless Bissell PowerClean DualBrush is designed for these routine cleanups, and it is currently on sale for $199.99 (originally $359.99). That is a $160 savings.Beyond pet-related messes, the PowerClean can also pick up crumbs, dust, tracked-in dirt, and other debris that accumulates between more thorough cleaning sessions. Because it converts from a standard stick vacuum into a handheld model and works with several attachments, you can move from cleaning floors to tackling furniture, stairs, and narrow spaces without reaching for a different machine. That versatility carries over to the way it cleans: Two self-cleaning brush rolls handle everything from scattered pet food to finer particles like fur and dust, while Bissell’s AutoAdapt system increases the suction when it detects a dirtier spot, allowing you to continue across the room without repeatedly stopping to manually change modes.The headlights on the floorhead add another practical touch, helping expose pale fur on rugs and fine dust on hard floors as you move around the room. That said, while Bissell says the battery can last up to 50 minutes, that estimate applies only when the detachable handheld vacuum is running in its lowest-power mode—and using stronger suction or the motorized floorhead will reduce that runtime. The 0.4-liter dust cup is another limitation, particularly in homes with several shedding pets, where it may need to be emptied during a longer cleaning session. These small compromises aside, the PowerClean will suit anyone who needs a cordless vacuum that can cover floors, stairs, furniture, and pet beds without requiring much setup or a full-size machine, especially at its current $160 discount.

title: Google May Be Working on a New Fitbit
body:
Beth Skwarecki
                            
        
            Beth Skwarecki
                
                                            Senior Health Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceBeth Skwarecki is Lifehacker’s Senior Health Editor, and holds certifications as a personal trainer and weightlifting coach. She has been writing about health for over 10 years.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        October 5, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    We may earn a commission from links on this page.
    
            The Fitbit Air, left (launched 2026) and the Fitbit Charge 6, right (launched 2023)
                                                    Credit: Beth Skwarecki
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Leaked images and spec sheets suggest Google is working on a "Fitbit Edge" device.
                                            The new device appears to have a slim screen set into a wristband, like the old Charge 6.
                                            No price or release date has been announced.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        A new Google wearable may be on the way, and leaked pictures suggest it may be a fitness band with a screen, a successor to the Fitbit Charge 6. Android Headlines reports that the new device will be called the Fitbit Edge. Earlier this year, Google ran ads on Reddit that seemed to show a new fitness band alongside Pixel watches and phones. In a post titled “Um so what the hell is that??,” redditors debated whether the unfamiliar wearable was an accidental leak of a yet-unreleased device, or just an AI hallucination. After all, if you asked an AI to create a hybrid of a Fitbit and a Pixel Watch, it would look more or less like what was in the picture.What rumors say about the new "Fitbit Edge"The leaked photos appearing at Android Headlines look like the device from the ad. It has an oval screen, only about as wide as the wristband and taller than it is wide. The rounded edges and the style of watch band match aesthetically with Pixel Watches, while the overall form factor—a tall screen set into a thin wristband—fits the design of the old Fitbit Charge 6. 
According to spec sheets that were reportedly also included in the leak, the device will have GPS, an altimeter, and a seven-day battery life. That's the same battery life as the Charge 6, which had GPS but no altimeter. The new device is said to work with both iOS and Android, as the Fitbit Air does, rather than being Android-only like the Pixel Watch. The rumors do not include a price, a release date, or a full list of features.What this means, if trueIf it weren’t for the earlier ad—the one that many thought was a hallucination—I probably wouldn’t have expected Google to release a device like this at all. Its last fitness tracker with a screen was the Fitbit Charge 6 in 2023. The Fitbit Air makes sense since smart bands are having a moment, and the Fitbit Air is a really well-executed one. But I wasn’t sure if Google was interested in continuing the Fitbit line beyond that one device. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
It’s a good idea, I think. Small trackers are easy to wear (and forget you’re wearing), but sometimes you just want to be able to see the time on your wrist. If Google is smart, they’ll allow you to swap seamlessly between the new device and the screenless Fitbit Air. (Currently, you can pair one Pixel Watch and one Fitbit to your phone, but you can’t pair two different models of Fitbit.) I’m excited to see what Google has in mind for the new device, assuming the rumors are true about its size, shape, and capabilities. I was disappointed by all the things the Charge 6 couldn’t do, and I hope the new Fitbit doesn’t repeat those mistakes. For example, the Charge 6 can control the music that’s playing on your phone, but only if you pay for a YouTube Music subscription. Most fitness watches—including Garmin, Coros, and Suunto watches I’ve tried—will simply give you controls for whatever is playing on your phone, no matter what app it comes from. If it’s true that the new device also has its own GPS and altimeter, that’s also exciting—but I’m skeptical that Google will be able to stuff in high-quality versions of those components in the space available. The Charge 6, I found, had trouble getting a good GPS reading and a good heart rate reading at the same time. But the Fitbit Air is surprisingly small and capable for its size, so I’m looking forward to seeing what the new device might be able to do.

title: You Might Need to Replace Your iPhone 18 Pro Max
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        October 5, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Firdous Nazir/NurPhoto via Getty Images
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Some iPhone 18 Pro Max users cannot connect to AT&T's networks. Their iPhones show an "SOS" icon in the status bar, instead.
                                            While it's not clear what's causing the issue, affected units cannot be fixed, and must be swapped out through AT&T or Apple.
                                            Unaffected units on AT&T should immediately update to iOS 27.0.1, as well as install the latest carrier update, to prevent the issue.
                                            This is just one of four major issues users are reporting with the new iPhone 18 Pro line, though this issue only affects iPhone 18 Pro Max.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Your iPhone 18 Pro Max can do a lot. It has a variable aperture that lets you control the amount of light that hits the camera sensor; it can charge up to 50% of its battery in 15 minutes (with the right adapter, of course); and it can run all of Apple's latest AI features, thanks to the new A20 processor. But the 18 Pro Max is still, above all, a phone. If it can't connect to the cellular network, you no longer have an iPhone, but a glorified iPod touch. Unfortunately, that's the situation some iPhone 18 Pro Max users find themselves in. Despite being "the best" iPhone Apple has ever made, Apple confirmed that a "small number" of 18 Pro Max units—specifically on the AT&T carrier network—can no longer connect to cellular service, with the devices only displaying an "SOS" icon at the top of their screens. That's a pretty glaring issue: Without cellular service, you'll need a wifi connection to use any apps or features that require the internet and you'll lose the ability to make calls over cellular entirely. It's so bad that some users may not even be able to call 911.  What if my iPhone 18 Pro Max can connect to cellular service right now?If your iPhone 18 Pro Max has the ability to connect to cellular service, that doesn't mean you're in the clear. Just because there's nothing wrong with your unit yet, you can still be affected by the glitch, and you'll need to install the latest update, iOS 27.0.1, as well as the latest carrier update from AT&T, to ensure your 18 Pro Max won't be affected by these mysterious cellular issues in the future. That's what Apple told 9to5Mac in the following statement: “We have identified an issue affecting a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network that may cause a device to lose service and be unable to make calls. We released iOS 27.0.1 earlier this week and strongly encourage all iPhone 18 Pro Max users to update now, and are also issuing a carrier settings update today. These updates together are meant to help prevent this issue from occurring.”
While you can always install iOS 27.0.1 from Settings > General> Software Update, Apple says that the carrier update will install on its own at some point over the next 14 days. However, I'd advise manually installing it by heading to Settings > General > About. There won't be any confirmation that the carrier update installs, but rest assured, this process will ensure that it has. What if my iPhone 18 Pro Max cannot connect to cellular?Unfortunately, if your iPhone is already experiencing issues connecting to cellular service, there is no fix. The updates above only help with prevention; they cannot patch an iPhone 18 Pro Max that already can't reach the network. Unfortunately, the only solution is to swap out the unit with either Apple or AT&T. The good news is your store will make the trade for you free of charge, as it is a hardware defect covered under warranty. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
It's not clear why this issue is only affecting iPhone 18 Pro Maxes and not the standard iPhone 18 Pro, nor is it evident why only AT&T devices appear to be experiencing it. A possible point of failure: The iPhone 18 Pro Max uses a Qualcomm modem, while the iPhone 18 Pro uses Apple's proprietary C2 modem. Perhaps there's some flaw with Qualcomm's hardware specifically on the AT&T network. That's not to say the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro has been otherwise drama-free—far from it. As it happens, the 18 Pro (along with the 18 Pro Max) has also experienced three other public-facing issues since Apple launched the devices last month. First, there was an issue with phones randomly rebooting following a failed Face ID attempt; next, some users noticed their devices emitting a cracking or popping sound through the speakers. Finally, some units also appear to be losing their exterior color. If you've upgraded, I hope your fancy new iPhone is doing well.

title: Amazon's New 'About You' Page Lists Everything It Knows About You
description:

        It shouldn't come as a surprise that Amazon collects data about you based on w
body:
We may earn a commission from links on this page.
    
        
        It shouldn't come as a surprise that Amazon collects data about you based on what you buy. And now, you can get a direct look at what the company has concluded from all that activity.Amazon's "About You" page, currently in beta after launching this May, uses data from customers' activity to generate details about them in categories like Product Preferences, Interests & Hobbies, and Home & Family. Amazon uses those details to personalize the shopping experience. Here's how to navigate and personalize your "About You" page in your Amazon account.What Amazon thinks it knows about youThe results can be oddly specific. My editor-in-chief, Jordan Calhoun, shared his page, which includes these entries:
"Likely has 2 adults""Owns a PlayStation 5 console""Prioritizes plant-based meat alternatives over traditional options""Subscribes to multiple streaming services continually""Owns a large dog""Likely has a cat"Full disclosure: I try to never use Amazon personally. I pretty much exclusively use it to round up deals for you, my dear reader. That being said, here's what Amazon thinks it knows about me: "Values durable travel gear," "prefers athletic and casual clothing styles," "practices yoga regularly," and "listens to music frequently."What counts as dataIn its Privacy Notice, Amazon lists every activity that provides user data to the company. That includes the obvious, like searching for items and placing orders. It also includes actions you may not realize are being tracked, like interacting with Alexa Voice Service, participating in discussion boards, or linking an Amazon account to a third-party business.How to view your own "About you" pageOn desktop:Hover over where Amazon says "Hello, [your name]" in the upper right corner.Under the "Your Account" section, click "Account."Under the "Ordering and shopping preferences" section, click "Your Shopping preferences."From here, you can add information of your own, like your shoe size, interests, and dietary preferences. Scroll to the bottom of the page, and you'll see a blue hyperlinked option that says, "Manage your information." Click it, and you'll see what dirt Amazon has on you.On the mobile app:
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Tap the hamburger icon in the bottom menu bar, then go to Account > Shopping preferences > About you.You can edit it, but not opt outShoppers can't directly opt out of the "About you" feature. They can, however, customize the data by adding details they want Amazon to know and deleting assumptions they consider inaccurate or too personal.Importing data from other AI chatbotsOn the "About you" page, customers also have the option to "make Amazon even more personal to you" by importing personal data they've shared with other AI agents. Amazon provides a prompt for you to feed to your chatbot to generate a shopping profile, then asks you to copy the bot's response and paste it back into Amazon.Whether that's worth doing is up to you. Given how much Amazon already infers from your browsing and buying, handing over a profile from another AI service is a choice worth thinking through. Either way, taking a few minutes to review your page and delete anything inaccurate or too personal is a simple way to see and shape what Amazon knows about you.

        Amazon's October Prime Day sale has dropped the Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar to $679 from its usual $999, taking $320 off and bringing it to the lowest price we've seen so far, according to price trackers. PCMag rated the Smart Ultra "outstanding," highlighting its ability to deliver surprisingly immersive Dolby Atmos audio without requiring a room full of additional speakers. If you don't need Bose's top-tier model, there's a less expensive Prime Day option as well: the Bose Smart Dolby Atmos Soundbar, which sits below the Smart Ultra in the lineup, is down to $399 from $549.
The Smart Ultra uses a 5.1.2-channel design with nine drivers, including two upward-firing drivers that bounce sound off the ceiling to create height effects. In practice, that means movies, TV shows, and games feel larger and more spacious than they do through most single-bar setups. Bose also includes its AdaptiQ room-calibration system, which measures your room's acoustics and adjusts the sound accordingly. The process takes a few minutes, but it helps the soundbar perform better across different spaces rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all tuning profile. The soundbar also works as a smart speaker, with Amazon Alexa built in and support for Apple AirPlay 2, Google Cast, Spotify Connect, Bluetooth, and multi-room audio through the Bose app.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Its biggest compromise is bass—for a single soundbar, its low end is respectable, but it can't fully replace what a dedicated subwoofer brings to action movies, concerts, or bass-heavy music. The good news is that Bose allows you to expand the system later with compatible wireless subwoofers and surround speakers if you decide you want more impact. For anyone looking for a premium one-piece soundbar that delivers convincing Dolby Atmos effects, clear dialogue, built-in smart features, and a much larger soundstage than TV speakers can provide, the Smart Ultra remains one of the strongest standalone options available, especially at this price.

        October Prime Day is here, and if you're looking for a versatile Android tablet, TCL's NXTPAPER 14, with a massive matte screen with different viewing modes for reading, streaming video, and writing, is 30% off during the sale. 
With a 14.3-inch display, the NXTPAPER 14 might not be as portable as other tablets on the market, but the screen itself is the biggest perk. The matte display has a paper-like feel and three different viewing modes: You can switch from black-and-white Ink Paper Mode to Color Paper Mode (a must for comics) to full color (for streaming video or using other full-motion apps) with the push of a button. Under harsh, direct lighting, it does an impressive job of reducing glare and reflections. It also has 8GB of RAM, 256GB of storage, and a large 10,000mAh battery. TCL claims up to 10.8 hours of video playback, though actual battery life will vary depending on use.The tablet comes with a folio-style case with a magnetic cover that doubles as a stand, a long charging cable, and a pressure-sensitive rechargeable stylus called the T-Pen, which offers 4,096 levels of pressure sensitivity. Combined with the matte texture of the display, the T-Pen creates a distinctive drag that you don’t get when using an Apple Pencil on an untreated glass screen. The tablet also has a useful Edge Bar feature: Swipe inward from the edge and hold to reveal a customizable mini dock containing shortcuts and tools. The 14.3-inch display makes these productivity features particularly useful, giving you enough room to keep reference material, notes, and other apps visible at once.The NXTPAPER 14 isn't a true e-ink device; it remains a backlit LCD, so it won’t provide Kindle-like battery life or outdoor visibility, but the matte screen aims to be easier on your eyes. Its 60Hz refresh rate is also less fluid than the screens on many premium tablets, and it lacks a microSD slot to expand the included 256GB of storage. Whether you’re an artist, love sketching or reading comics, need to review and sign documents, or simply want a larger screen without all the bells and whistles of a premium tablet, the sizable NXTPAPER 14 is an excellent multitasking canvas with some of the reading and writing benefits associated with paper-like displays without the limitations of e-ink.Amazon October Prime Day FAQWhat time does Prime Day start?October Prime Day starts Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 12:00 a.m. PT / 3:00 a.m. ET.

        Wireless charging is convenient, but faster speeds can generate more heat, potentially putting additional strain on your phone’s battery over time. The Anker Prime 3-in-1 MagSafe Charger is designed to manage that heat while keeping charging speeds high, and for October Prime Day 2026, it’s down to $132.98 from $229.99, its lowest price to date, according to price trackers. The setup is aimed squarely at Apple users, with dedicated charging spots for an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods in one compact station.
Its main pad supports 25W Qi2 wireless charging, which is about as fast as cable-free charging gets right now, and it’s paired with a built-in thermoelectric cooling system and fan to keep temperatures under control, as noted in this ZDNET review. That cooling system actively pulls heat away from your phone while it charges, so you can charge while streaming or scrolling without the phone getting uncomfortably warm. There are three charging modes you can choose from: Boost Mode is for quick top-ups when you’re heading out, Ice Mode keeps things cooler during heavier use, and Sleep Mode slows everything down and turns off the fan for overnight charging. The pad also tilts up to 80 degrees, so it doubles as a stand for watching videos or taking calls.

        A GoPro is great for capturing footage, but not so much if you get frustrated lugging it around on your adventures. That’s the advantage of the GoPro Lit Hero: At just 3.3 ounces, it’s small enough to slip into a jacket pocket or keep clipped to a bike helmet. And for October Prime Day, the Lit Hero is down to $179.95 from its $270 launch price, the lowest price recorded by price trackers so far. For more on the October Prime Day sale, you can follow offers as they come in on our Prime Day 2026 Live Blog or browse our Prime Day Deals coverage.It records up to 4K at 60fps, captures 12MP photos, and is waterproof down to 16 feet without needing extra housing, making it practical for casual travel, cycling, beach trips, or quick vacation clips. Startup speeds are fast, autofocus works reliably, and the battery lasts around 90 minutes of continuous shooting (the battery is sealed and cannot be swapped out mid-day). The built-in LED light is also brighter than expected for a camera this small, although it feels more useful underwater or during emergencies than for everyday clips.
On the minus side, its 1.76-inch touchscreen is extremely small, and navigating menus can be tricky, especially if you're outdoors or have wet hands. Because there are barely any physical controls, almost everything depends on tapping through menus on that tiny display. There’s also no built-in image stabilization; instead, you have to transfer footage into the GoPro Quik app and apply stabilization afterward, which adds an extra step. While the image quality is decent in bright conditions, the small 1/2.8-inch sensor struggles in dimmer environments, producing softer footage with visible noise. If you're into color grading or tweaking your footage later, you won’t get much flexibility here either, since there’s no log mode or meaningful manual control to work with. Overall, the Lit Hero feels less like a smaller Hero Black and more like a compact point-and-shoot action camera for beginners who care more about convenience and size than image quality—but if those are major factors for you, it's a good bet at the current discount.How does Prime Day work?Prime Day lets Prime Members shop online for thousands of products with big discounts.
